question: Can a single bounded function that makes the curvature exponent depend on measured baryonic mass, local density, or distribution shape improve galaxy and cluster predictions without per-object gravity parameters?

sample.bridge_objective: equal-domain mean of equal-system mean squared log residual
sample.SPARC: 131 galaxies; nuisance parameters fit on 2066 inner points and tested on 968 untouched outer points
sample.raw_lensing: RX J2129 image-position diagnostic for the three predeclared models; local density for raw profiles is the spherical derivative of the baryonic force profile

curvature_variable_mass_power.X: spherical-equivalent enclosed baryonic mass in solar masses, M_eq=g_bar r^2/G

curvature_variable_density_power.X: local baryonic volume density in g/cm^3

curvature_variable_shape_power.X: local baryonic density divided by spherical-equivalent mean enclosed baryonic density

solar_gates.interpretation: This remains a phenomenological zero-slip proxy rather than a relativistic derivation. Cassini directly constrained gamma, not a running G.

selection.primary_rule: fit all five universal gravity parameters only to the five-fold BCG+cluster bridge; SPARC is transfer-only
selection.post_transfer_warning: comparisons among these candidates become exploratory after SPARC inspection
